summary: Analysis of 14 days of continuous glucose monitoring data reveals excellent overall glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and a low coefficient of variation of 12.9%. No hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) was recorded. Baseline basal rates, CR, ISF, and automated SMB/UAM loop delivery are well-calibrated. The main opportunity for refinement is addressing transient postprandial glucose spikes during weekend brunches (peaking up to 188 mg/dL) by optimizing prebolus timing and initial bolus distribution.

analysis_steps.findings: 1,345 CGM entries over 14 days provide 100.0% coverage without data gaps and a consistent 15-minute sampling cadence. 32 treatment records and active AAPS profile settings are fully logged.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries out of 1,345 expected; 0 gaps > 15 min; 28 carb treatments and 28 insulin treatments recorded.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic stability is exceptional. Mean glucose is 117.0 mg/dL with a standard deviation of 15.1 mg/dL. Time in Range is 99.7%, Time Above Range (>180 mg/dL) is 0.3%, and Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) is 0.0%.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL; CV 12.9%; 0 events below 70 mg/dL across 14 days; maximum glucose 188.0 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain stable baseline glucose near target (102.3-107.5 mg/dL average between 00:00 and 05:00 local time) without upward or downward drift.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight hourly averages stay within 102.3-107.5 mg/dL, tightly aligned with the target window of 95-110 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Carbohydrate ratios, ISF, and DIA (5.5 hours) are well-tuned. Weekday breakfast and dinner postprandial curves return smoothly to baseline within 240-360 minutes without late hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast 120m change is +33 to +57 mg/dL returning to baseline at 240m; dinner 120m change is +15 to +41 mg/dL returning to baseline at 240m.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM delivery parameters are effectively controlling postprandial excursions without causing over-correction low glucose events.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM enabled; 3 min SMB interval; 45 min max SMB basal; 30 min max UAM SMB basal; 0.0% time below range.
data_gaps: Raw settings for specific SMB UI activation triggers (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled) are unlogged (null) in export context.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits and sensitivity settings are appropriately proportioned. Max basal (2.4 U/h) and Max IOB (8.0 U) provide required headroom without excessive accumulation risk.
analysis_steps.evidence: Max basal 2.4 U/h (~2.3x max profile basal 1.05 U/h); Max IOB 8.0 U vs max single meal bolus 5.8 U; Dynamic ISF factor 100%.
data_gaps: Autosens enablement flags are unlogged (null) in raw export metadata.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekday meal timing (20 min prebolus, 70% upfront) is highly effective. Weekend brunch (10 min prebolus, 60% upfront) allows a brief spike to 188 mg/dL due to higher carb volume and lower initial prebolus timing.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunches peak at 188 mg/dL (+62 to +70 mg/dL at 120m), accounting for all 0.3% TAR in the period, but recover to 111-119 mg/dL by 240m.

analysis_steps.findings: The declared e-carb strategy for weekend brunch (20g e-carbs over 120 min starting at +15 min offset) accurately captures late absorption from mixed meals, preventing late postprandial highs.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose settles to 111-119 mg/dL at 240m and 111-113 mg/dL at 360m after weekend brunches without secondary spikes.

analysis_steps.findings: The overall control strategy is operating with high efficacy and safety. Profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, DIA) and AAPS limits require no structural changes. The primary optimization is behavioral: lengthening the prebolus for weekend brunch to attenuate early postprandial spikes.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined telemetry across 14 days shows 99.7% TIR, 0.0% TBR, 12.9% CV, stable overnight glucose, and postprandial peaks limited to weekend brunch hours.

strengths: Outstanding Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL).
Highly stable overnight fasting glucose averaging 102-107 mg/dL, confirming precise nocturnal basal calibration.
Low glycemic variability with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9% and Standard Deviation of 15.1 mg/dL.
Effective integration of SMB and UAM automated delivery managing meal recovery without hypoglycemia.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose peaks up to 188 mg/dL following weekend brunches (10:30) due to a shortened 10-minute prebolus and 60% immediate bolus split on higher-carbohydrate mixed meals.

recommendations.title: Optimize Weekend Brunch Prebolus Timing
recommendations.description: Weekend brunches currently show an early glucose peak reaching 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes post-meal. Extending the prebolus from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes or increasing the upfront bolus split from 60% to 70% can curb this peak while keeping the 20g e-carb entry to handle late absorption.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile segments deliver 99.7% TIR with 0.0% hypoglycemia and stable overnight fasting glucose. Postprandial excursions are limited and best addressed by prebolus timing rather than ratio shifts.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe 60-minute and 120-minute postprandial glucose trends during the next two weekend brunches after testing a 15-minute prebolus.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Keep all core AAPS profile parameters (basal rates, CR, ISF, DIA, and Targets) unchanged.
Step 2: Verify in the AAPS user interface that SMB activation conditions and Autosens options match your preferred configuration.
Step 3: For upcoming weekend brunches, trial a 15-minute prebolus (increased from 10 minutes) or increase upfront bolus percentage to 70%, keeping the 20g e-carb entry.
Step 4: Monitor postprandial glucose curves at 60 and 120 minutes following the adjusted brunch prebolus to confirm reduction in peak glucose.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain a 20-minute prebolus with a 70% immediate bolus ratio for standard meals, leveraging SMB/UAM for residual absorption. Use e-carbs (20g over 120 min) for higher-fat or mixed meals.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Standard meals show ideal postprandial curves with 20 min prebolus and 70% upfront split. E-carbs accurately model delayed absorption for mixed meals without late highs.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe post-brunch peak glucose after extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Increase prebolus from 10 to 15-20 minutes and test a 70% upfront bolus split while retaining 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes.
exceptions.rationale: Curbs the early peak (188 mg/dL at 120m) while e-carbs protect against late glucose rises.

education: Prebolus timing allows rapid-acting insulin to begin working before carbohydrate absorption starts, attenuating early postprandial peaks.

Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) inform the closed-loop algorithm about delayed gastric emptying in high-fat/high-protein meals, preventing premature over-dosing while ensuring automated delivery remains active later.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content for review only and does not constitute medical advice.
